sentences.sentence: 2017 Hall of Fame dinner.
I've been to this event about once every year for the past ten years.
It's never been a particularly glamorous evening.
And this was one of the least glamorous of them all.
No celebrity speaker, although there was a band playing.
The meal, according to several guests, was the most mediocre of the lot.
The highlight of the evening was a video introduction of Barack Obama, who reminded the audience that he won Iowa in 2008 and that's not something that's going to happen again anytime soon.
It was, however, a record-setting crowd.
As you would expect, Iowa Democratic Party chair Andy McGuire was understandably pleased, describing it as "the most important" gathering of state Democrats in 50 years.

The Des Moines Register reported "there were also the usual signs that times are changing in Iowa: young professionals and some minority faces, an audience that's more diverse than the previous eight Hall of Fame dinners."
McGuire said the event raised $445,000 for the party, which may be a record for a Hall of Fame dinner as well.
McGuire has made clear that he believes the party is still in a fundraising deficit from the Obama era, and that he needs big bucks to prepare for the 2018 campaign.
This would appear to be the first step in that direction.
The party's fundraising efforts received a substantial boost last week.

The state's seven Democratic representatives in the House of Representatives received some national support from EMILY's List, which raised more than $750,000 to support Democratic women in the last cycle of races.
Among those receiving funding was Des Moines-based congresswoman Cindy Axne, who got a $10,000 donation from the group, which supports abortion-rights candidates.
